evidence.dayUnit: ED timeline text: 'within 15 working days of online receipt by the Chief Inspector's office; this extends to 30 working days for factories carrying out hazardous processes' — ed_data/UP.json
evidence.clockBehaviour: The published Government Order fixes query conduct but not the effect on the overall limit: a maximum of one query 'within 07 working days' of the application reaching the portal, and 'if no query is sent within 07 working days, the application is automatically deemed free of deficiency' — via secondary_data/UP.json
evidence.authority: The ED attributes the figure to 'Factories Act, 1948 (Section 2(cb)) / Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (Rule 2(ja))', but the published-rules lane records that 'No 15-day figure, and no hazardous/non-hazardous split, appears anywhere in the Labour Department block of the published table' — ed_data/UP.json, secondary_data/UP.json
evidence.promisedOrExperienced: 'The plan of a factory must be disposed of within 15 working days of online receipt' — a limit; the FGD lane carries no timeline at all — ed_data/UP.json, fgd_data/UP.json

UP.reason: What the 15/30 figure covers is disputed between the lanes, and the statutory basis the ED cites for it is not borne out by the published table.
UP.note: UP is the only State in the set with a clean day unit and no usable scope: it is the mirror image of the common failure, and the published-rules lane is what exposed it.

evidence.journeyScope: The ED's five steps run from 'Submit Factory Licence application' to 'Licence issued'; the antecedent plan stage is evidenced by the ED finding 'The factory building/layout plan must be resubmitted at renewal even when there has been no change in layout or infrastructure' and by Factories Act s.6(1)(aa), 'requiring, the previous permission in writing of the State Government or the Chief Inspector to be obtained for the site on which the factory is to be situated and for the construction or extension of any factory' — ed_data/WB.json and secondary_data/WB.json
evidence.dayUnit: NOT established. The published-rules lane's holiday-exclusion text is expressly conditional: "If WB's Factory Licence limit is an RTPS-notified limit, 65 'days' is therefore a holiday-excluded clock that restarts on deficiency correction". The condition is unmet: that file's timeline check carries the verdict not_found with a null sourceSays and a null citation, and the ED itself records 'exact governing Act/Rule and average actual timeline not specified' — ed_data/WB.json, secondary_data/WB.json
evidence.clockBehaviour: Same conditional defect: rule 4(1) of the WB Right to Public Services Rules, 2013 ('the stipulated time limit for such service shall start from the date of production of the document') only bites if the 65 is an RTPS-notified limit, which is unproven — secondary_data/WB.json
evidence.authority: ED timeline basis: 'Approximate figure discussed by the expert; exact governing Act/Rule and average actual timeline not specified' — ed_data/WB.json
evidence.promisedOrExperienced: Neither: the basis field rules out both readings at once — the governing Act/Rule is 'not specified' (so it is not a promise on record) and the 'average actual timeline' is likewise 'not specified' (so it is not an observed duration) — ed_data/WB.json

WB.reason: The 65 is an approximate expert figure whose governing instrument is expressly unidentified, so neither its day unit nor its clock behaviour can be fixed.
WB.note: This classification deliberately departs from the worked example in the spec, which assigns WB dayUnit 'working-holidays-excluded', clockBehaviour 'resets', confidence 'high' and determinable true. The underlying validation does not support that: secondary_data/WB.json records the timeline check as 'not_found' ('THE 65-DAY FIGURE COULD NOT BE VERIFIED OR REFUTED'), every West Bengal government host was unreachable, and the rule 5 / rule 4(1) quotations appear only inside an explicitly conditional remark. On the spec's own grouping rule, an official-estimate with no stated basis is not-comparable.

calibration.verdict: Do not extend this to the other 24 licences as it stands. Only 6 of 22 Factory Licence records could be placed in a comparable group, and the reason is almost entirely one dimension: 15 of 22 records never say whether their days are calendar or working, so a State can have a notified instrument, a published SOP and a settled clock rule (Jharkhand, Jammu & Kashmir, Delhi) and still be unchartable. Four of the six determinable States — DNHDD, MN, MP and PY — owe their day unit or their figure entirely to the published-rules lane, so on the only licence that has that lane, it is doing two-thirds of the work; on the 24 licences without it the determinable share would plausibly fall to the 2-in-22 the field records alone supported here. The honest recommendation is to spend the next tranche on fixing the instrument rather than widening it: add a mandatory 'days are calendar/working, and here is the phrase that says so' field to the ED and FGD protocols, and commission the published-rules validation for the licences before the fieldwork rather than after, since it changed or supplied a dimension in 10 of the 15 States where it existed.

remarks: RULE APPLIED FOR dayUnit: assigned only where a source uses an explicit unit word ('working days', 'calendar days', 'excluding public holidays') or states the limit in an inherently calendar unit ('one month', '3 months'). Everything else is 'unclear', including business-reported lived durations such as Maharashtra's 'about forty to fifty days'. This is the strict reading the spec requires; a laxer convention treating every experienced elapsed duration as calendar would move HR, MH and arguably AR and NL into comparable groups, taking determinable from 6 to about 10. Both numbers are given so the Council can choose the convention rather than inherit mine.

THE SPEC'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE DOES NOT SURVIVE VERIFICATION. The WB example in the spec cites 'WB RTPS Rules 2013 rule 5' and 'rule 4(1)' as settling dayUnit and clockBehaviour 'via secondary_data/WB.json' with confidence 'high'. Those phrases are in that file, but only inside a remark that begins 'If WB's Factory Licence limit is an RTPS-notified limit' — and the file's own timeline check is verdict 'not_found', sourceSays null, citation null, because every West Bengal government host was unreachable. One of the three cases the spec calls 'already proven from official sources' is therefore not proven. The other two (NL final-leg, MN working days) are fully supported by the data.

statedMin/statedMax are kept as the FIELD record's figure wherever one exists, with published-rules conflicts recorded in the note rather than overwriting the number — this follows the spec's WB example, which keeps 65. Where the field record has no figure at all, the published figure was used and the note says so: DL (60), MP (7). CG's 30 comes from an FGD finding, not from its ED record, which carries null.

RANGES THAT ARE NOT RANGES. Three records carry a statedMin and statedMax that measure different things, and a min-max whisker on the dashboard would misrepresent all three: RJ 15-60 is three category services (15 non-hazardous / 21 hazardous / 60 MAH); AS 15-45 is a pre-use application window, a Citizen's Charter standard and a Rules standard that the record says are unreconciled; UP 15-30 is a non-hazardous and a hazardous plan-disposal limit.

THE GROUPING SCHEME HAS NO SLOT FOR applicant-inclusive. Kerala's 90-120 days runs 'from initial building-plan preparation to final approval' and includes the applicant's own engineer-engagement time and other departments' clearances; it lands in full-journey-calendar by the spec's rules but is materially wider than anything else that would sit there. Its own State's notified comparator is 50 days. Recommend a fifth group, or an explicit applicant-inclusive flag, before anything is charted.

PROMISE AND EXPERIENCE ARE BEING MIXED ON ONE AXIS. Of the 22, 13 records carry a promised standard and 6 carry a lived duration; PB is the extreme case, carrying 30 as its figure while the same record states approvals 'take 1 year or more in practice'. comparisonGroup does not separate these, so even within full-journey-calendar a promised figure and an experienced figure are not comparable. Recommend splitting each group by promisedOrExperienced.

clockBehaviour was the weakest dimension overall — 17 of 22 unclear — but it is not part of the determinability test, so it did not cost any State a group. It is worth noting that all five States where it WAS settled (DNHDD, JH, JK, KL, MP) were settled by a published rule or by a lane other than the timeline field itself, which is the strongest single argument for commissioning the published-rules validation earlier.

THE SIX DETERMINABLE STATES ARE NOT SIX SOLID STATES. Only MN is high confidence. DNHDD, KL, MP and PY are medium (DNHDD's scope conflicts with its own notified per-service limits; KL's scope is wider than the group allows; MP's figure is absent from the field record entirely; PY's day unit rests on a notified order saying 'one month' rather than counting days), and AP is low — its determinability turns on the single word 'statutory' with no instrument named and no second lane to check it. A dashboard built on this set would be charting one properly evidenced State.

Four States where the two field lanes flatly disagree are recorded in the dataset's own INCONSISTENT flags and are reflected in the confidence values here: AP (statutory 7 days vs no published timeline visible to applicants), CG (ED has no figure, FGD reports 30), DNHDD (ED says no deemed approval, FGD says 25-day deemed approval — the published order settles it at 20 working days), JK (ED cites a PSGA 30-day limit, FGD participants had never heard of any timeline).
